sentences.text: Solicitor Rachel Dunne confirmed confidentiality and legal privilege for the conversation.
Client Matthew Kerr described being touched by Brian Hollis, who ran the junior squad at Harbridge Swimming Club, in the changing room after training when other children had left.
Matthew Kerr disclosed that Brian Hollis made him touch Hollis, stating it was part of being in the squad and that everyone did it.
Matthew Kerr stated the incidents occurred every Saturday morning after squad training for approximately two years, from when he was eleven until nearly thirteen (roughly 1996 to 1
Matthew Kerr reported that he told his mother when he was 13; she took him out of the club but did not report it to anyone.
Matthew Kerr disclosed that he told his wife Claire in 2020, his GP, and went to the police in March of the previous year, providing a statement.
Matthew Kerr stated the police officer interviewed Brian Hollis and the investigation is still ongoing.
Matthew Kerr reported hearing that Brian Hollis had done it to other boys, including a lad in the squad who messaged him on Facebook saying he heard the same from a couple of other
Matthew Kerr stated he never saw anything happen to anyone else himself.
Matthew Kerr disclosed he has had anxiety for years and panic attacks, receiving counselling through work in 2021.
Matthew Kerr stated he is a site manager and had three months off sick in 2021.
Matthew Kerr provided the name of the police officer as DC Farrow.
Matthew Kerr confirmed he has sick notes and a letter from his counsellor.
Matthew Kerr stated his objectives are: 1) for the club to admit it and say they let it happen; 2) money for counselling due to NHS waiting list issues.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne explained that normally there is a three-year time limit for personal injury claims, which for a child starts at eighteen, but in abuse cases the court can允许
Solicitor Rachel Dunne advised that a claim could be against Brian Hollis himself and against the club if he was acting as their coach.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne advised that the solicitor would act on a no win, no fee agreement.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne advised Matthew Kerr to look after himself and suggested contacting his counsellor or GP for support, and offered details of a support service for survivors.
Matthew Kerr agreed to send the crime reference, DC Farrow's details, the counsellor's letter, and the sick notes by Friday 4 December.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne stated she would request Matthew Kerr's GP records with his permission and send a form to sign this week.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne stated she would write to the police to ask about the investigation and send the client care letter and funding agreement by Monday 30 December.
Solicitor Rachel Dunne scheduled a follow-up conversation for 10 December.
